data.bottom_line: The Central Oregon Avalanche Center is scheduled to begin avalanche forecasting on December 1. Hopefully we'll have enough snow to ride in the monument by then! For the Paulina zone we issue avalanche forecasts for every Saturday and Sunday, and usually publish a mid-week observation. As we start getting drips and drabs of early season snow, check out both our observations page as well as our weather station map for conditions. If we do pick up enough snow for some early season riding, remember that avalanches are possible even in relatively shallow snowpacks. This means that if there is enough snow to ride a sled, or make good turns, treat your travel as you would mid-winter; carry avalanche rescue gear, use thoughtful travel techniques, and assess the snow conditions. Places where you'll find the best early season riding like wind blown deposits are also where you are most likely to find avalanches. During November and December the avalanche center has lots of pre-season events scheduled to help you build enthusiasm for the season! Here is a link to our events page: https://coavalanche.org/pages/events .
